hooks._comment_sessionstart: FLEET DOCTRINE CURRENCY, wired 2026-08-30. Bus law 3 says 'pull at boot and wake ticks'. That was prose and produced zero pulls: this box's bus clone was found 229 commits behind origin/master with a clean git status, and tools/doctrine-sync.mjs - which implements the check correctly - was invoked by NOTHING anywhere in the fleet. This hook is the boot half. It ends in '|| exit 0' ON PURPOSE: doctrine-sync exits 1 when folding is owed, and a non-zero SessionStart hook can abort session start, so the loudness here is the TEXT landing in the agent's context, not the exit code. The hard non-zero signal lives in the machine-scoped scheduled task MLV-FleetDoctrineSweep, which runs tools/fleet-sweep.mjs across every member. The bus path is absolute and machine-specific - same known debt as the interpreter pin above, and deliberate for the same reason: a portable-but-wrong command fails open.
hooks._comment_resume_readiness: RESUME-READINESS, wired 2026-09-02 before a planned account rotation. Runs after every turn and PRINTS NOTHING unless a resume surface is stale, so it costs no tokens on the happy path. It checks the four surfaces a fresh session actually reads: the heartbeat snapshot (1 h bound - its own contract is 30 min), the SESSION-HANDOFF anchor, the NEWEST *-resume-CURRENT.md by mtime (never a named one - naming one is how the memory trigger went stale), and RESUME.md's derived-value contract. IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT GATED ON A USAGE THRESHOLD: weekly usage percentage is not persisted anywhere readable on this box, so an 89% trigger would be a gate that never fires - a policy on a path the live arm never reaches. Running it unconditionally is cheaper than detecting, and removes the surprise entirely. The script lives under .claude-state/ ON PURPOSE, like the board heartbeat: a tracked script vanishes when the checkout moves to a ref that predates it, which is exactly how all three hooks here broke on 2026-08-30.
